description.narrative: In its second year of implementation, OHK is funding two key initiatives in Vietnam for FY25/26 with a totalbudget of USD 190,000 (approximately HKD 1,482,000): the Tea Value Chain Project in Thai Nguyen provinceand the Fair Finance Project in Le Thuy district.Tea value chain projectThe Tea Value Chain Project, with a budget of USD 153,550, focuses on enhancing the sustainability,climate resilience, and gender responsiveness of tea production in Dai Tu, Dinh Hoa, and Dong Hy districts.Tea is a vital agricultural product in Vietnam, supporting 2.5 million farmers and ranking 10th globally inexports. In Thai Nguyen, tea cultivation spans 22,200 hectaresand employs nearly half the province’spopulation. While green tea is sold domestically, black tea is exported to markets such as Pakistan andChina. However, the sector faces significant challenges, including fragmented production, low adoption ofsustainable standards (only 25% of products are certified), climate vulnerability, and limited access tofinance—particularly for ethnic minorities and women. Fair Finance projectThe Fair Finance Project, with a budget of USD 36,450, is being implemented in Le Thuy district, whereaccess to financial services remains limited—especially for poor ethnic minority women.These groups facebarriers such as complex loanprocedures, mortgage requirements, and low loan limits, which hinderfarming expansion. Many resort to informal lenders charging exorbitant interest rates of up to 360%annually, often accompanied by threats and harassment. Digital financial literacy is also low, leaving ruralresidents vulnerable to scams and excluded from online banking services. The project begins with aresearch phase to assess current financial service usage and identify gaps. A core group of 8–10 members,65% of whom are women including ethnic minorities, will be trained in financial inclusion, serviceknowledge, coordination, and communication. This group will lead quarterly planningand monitoringmeetings, compile a handbook on accessing financial services, and facilitate policy dialogue with localauthorities and financial institutions. A community event will be organized to connect residents withregulators and private sector actors, promoting safe, inclusive, and effective financial services. The projectaims to reach 125 people, including 80 community members.

participating-org.narrative: In Vietnam , Oxfam is one of the leading international, non -governmental organisation. Since 1955, Oxfam is active in Vietnam withhumanitarian interventions and started development work in the late 1980's. Today, Oxfam works in 26 provinces with people, governments and civil society to promote equality and well-being through social and economic change.
